html:
A trade union leader who led Guinea to independence in 1958 and was its president until his death in 1984.

His Democratic Party of Guinea won the No vote against France. He was a leading voice of Pan-Africanism, gave the exiled Nkrumah a home and helped the PAIGC fight the Portuguese. At home he built a one-party socialist state, saw plots everywhere, and jailed, tortured and killed thousands of opponents, many at Camp Boiro. Hundreds of thousands of Guineans fled abroad. He died in a hospital in the United States in March 1984, and the army seized power a week later under Lansana Conte.
sum: A trade union leader who led Guinea to independence in 1958 and was its president until his death in 1984.
